Two of Dubai's most quoted gold pages disagree this morning by AED 10.80 a gram — and neither one is wrong.

LivePriceOfGold's board reads AED 512.45 a gram for 24-carat gold. Goodreturns' page, dated the same morning, reads AED 523.25. That is a gap of 2.11% before anyone has cut anything.

Kitco's live spot at 5:57am New York time puts gold at $4,341.40 an ounce — $139.58 a gram, or AED 512.59 at the dirham's fixed peg, both derived by this desk. One page sits three hundredths of a per cent from that line. The other sits AED 10.66 above it. One is publishing the metal. The other, the counter.

A jeweller quoting off one page and buying off the other is out by a meaningful part of a making charge before the scissors come out. The instruction: stop quoting 'the Dubai gold rate' as a single number, and state the peg arithmetic beside it.

India hallmarked 5.9 million silver articles in the financial year just ended — nearly double the 3.2 million the year before, an increase of about 84% derived by this desk.

The Bureau of Indian Standards named the cause plainly: consumers moving into silver because gold has become unaffordable. About 230 recognised centres currently handle the testing, and the bureau says its own lab network — 440 laboratories, up from 147 in 2014 — needs roughly two more years to catch up with demand.

This is the volume number behind a substitution this paper has tracked all year from other angles: India's gold jewellery demand fell 15% by weight this quarter, and Kalyan Jewellers took over 46% of its June-quarter revenue in recycled gold. A consumer survey records intent. A retailer's revenue can move on price alone. An assay count cannot — every article in it physically exists and physically passed a test.

There is no mandatory hallmarking date for silver yet. The unique identification number the bureau introduced in September 2025 is the plumbing a mandatory regime would need — and it's already in place.

Etsy is cutting about 220 jobs — roughly 12% of its marketplace workforce — in a quarter it beat.

Revenue for the quarter came in at $668.3 million, up 6.2% year on year against a Wall Street consensus of $646.1 million. Active sellers grew 5.9% to 5.7 million. The company says the cuts, which fall mainly on product and engineering, are about structure rather than cost, and are not related to artificial intelligence.

The reason this belongs on a jewellery desk: jewellery and personal accessories is one of Etsy's largest categories by gross merchandise sales, and a large share of the world's independent jewellery makers reach their customers through this one company's search ranking, fee schedule and product decisions. Those decisions are now made by a smaller team — and active buyers already slipped 0.4% while sellers keep joining.

For any maker with meaningful revenue on the platform, the number worth holding isn't 220. It's 5.7 million sellers competing for a buyer count that just went slightly backwards.
